answer: Each agent identity must maintain a sealed data vault whose key material is unique to it. The ledger periodically issues a fresh delta challenge: decrypt a target cipher within a tight time bound, using only that vault's contents. One operator can keep only one vault's secrets hot at a time, so a sybil swarm of N fake identities needs N real vaults — faking identities costs as much as being N independent agents. Copying one vault across many identities fails: each delta challenge binds to a unique identity-cipher, and replayed decryptions are rejected on-ledger.
